translations.9f98422f4d58249cb04f652a: A complete intention has four parts; if any one is missing, the agent fills in the gap the way it sees fit.
translations.4aebca5a941a60682f7de05b: ⟪P0⟫What⟪P1⟫is good—how to recognize an acceptable result.
translations.e42272bada838e5157de7feb: ✓ Always write all four parts, even for small tasks.
translations.14e4764d372bacca9d29888f: ✗ Asking “take care of this for me” without saying what is good or what is prohibited.
translations.ebb692e914210f49da820322: Take a request you would make to AI today and write the four lines: what, what is good, limits, and when it ends.
translations.6f87a020e217f7e3326203a9: Example: what, confirm tomorrow’s consults; good, every patient received a message; limit, never reschedule; ends, at 5pm with the list of who didn’t respond. If you got stuck on any line, that’s where the agent would also get stuck.
translations.425fa8e4bf4b473ad06c9012: The seven steps group into four phases; the last one feeds learning back to the first.
translations.f72b9b381ac06fc2ef1ecd76: ⟪P0⟫Execute⟪P1⟫the agent acts within autonomy and guardrails.
translations.a27a9803e4440608e0372f8b: ⟪P0⟫Learn⟪P1⟫assess via the log, supervise, and evolve.
translations.bd462263c92899ac85e16e93: ✓ When there’s an error, first ask which step in the flow it was born from.
translations.d072ce0e802c0a55b2c5fb99: ✗ Switching AI tools after every error without looking at intention, context, and data.
translations.32d522690ce657358c774416: Recall an error the AI made with you and classify which of the seven steps it was born from.
translations.e681e35b6c61a09a2a2a54c4: In most cases, the error is born in Context or Data: a rule was missing or the information was outdated. The fix is usually one more line in the instructions, not a new tool.
translations.42f4cc6990d2dd7e61e3d33f: The three dimensions need a meeting point: a single list of agents with an owner and a defined process.
translations.9664262da4916a183b0a166a: ⟪P0⟫People⟪P1⟫who defines, approves, and is accountable for each agent.
translations.e728b89ee557070b811023a9: ⟪P0⟫Processes⟪P1⟫what routine the agent handles, from start to finish.
translations.6585bcdf84b24f49594d4a6e: ⟪P0⟫Agents⟪P1⟫what each one does—and what it doesn’t do.
translations.e792ae06a0de71a1f5b8a5f5: Agents: check the effect in the example.
translations.f728124e73bb4db2ea0a1057: Single list: record the output evidence.
translations.f0711dfcb206e0b1b46ce712: ✓ Keep a single list of agents, each with an owner named.
translations.2d89b984c86ffdcd53ff0760: ✗ Letting each person set up their own automation without telling anyone.
translations.fb81d5db3bace3b8e661afe3: Do the inventory above with at least three items, including simple automations such as an automatic email response.
translations.57d26ed25f1e965afcd5eba9: It’s common to discover forgotten automations or ones without an owner. An agent without an owner isn’t reviewed, and what isn’t reviewed ends up repeating errors without anyone noticing.
translations.83f27c34ae574230fdcdca9a: The first delegation follows four steps, and the level is a consequence of the answers, not a free choice.
